meta.title: robotcode repl / robot-debug input-format rules for a PreToolUse Bash hook
meta.verified_with: robotcode 2.7.0, Robot Framework 7.5, Browser 20.5, Python 3.13, Linux; stdin = pipe/heredoc (non-TTY) unless noted
meta.evidence_dir: round5/research/repl_format/logs (case ids below = log file names; jsonl = logs/repl_cases.jsonl)
meta.hook_contract: Match only Bash commands whose command position runs `robotcode [global opts] (repl|shell|robot-debug|run-debug)`. scope=command rules inspect the shell command; scope=input rules inspect the heredoc / piped / file body. action: autofix = rewrite tool input (Claude/Codex updatedInput, Copilot modifiedArgs, OpenCode output.args) and mention the fix in context; deny = block with message; warn = allow + additionalContext; info = only in the format card. Prototype: repl_format/repl_lint.py (applies these rules; 34 examples).

costs_measured.browser_keyword_with_missing_outputdir_s: ~16 per Browser keyword (B01: 33 s for 3 lines; old report: 112 s vs 9 s)
costs_measured.robot_debug_exit_code: = number of failed tests (1), 253 after .abort, 0 when all pass

meta.prototype_selftest: repl_format/repl_lint.py --selftest: 34/34; repl_format/validate_rewrites.py (logs/validate_rewrites.json): 15/15 rewritten commands ran clean live; 14/15 originals were wrong (11 with FAIL lines, 3 silently: quoted .kw found nothing, quoted .break never stopped, FAIL dropped by pipe).

rules.message: Added --plain: on a real PTY without an agent marker env var the prompt-toolkit backend swallows piped lines and hangs.
rules.evidence: S13_pty.log: PTY + no agent env -> 77 escape sequences, statement never executed, killed by timeout after 25 s; with --plain or AI_AGENT/CLAUDECODE/CODEX_*/OPENCODE set -> plain, 4.2 s. Pipes/heredocs are plain automatically (cli.py _resolve_backend).

rules.message: (silent) --no-history keeps agent sessions out of the user's REPL history.
rules.evidence: S05_history.log: plain backend wrote no history file anyway; harmless, idempotent.

detect.note: resolve a relative dir against the robotcode project root (nearest dir upwards with robot.toml, pyproject.toml or .git; --root/ROBOTCODE_ROOT override), NOT the shell cwd; with no -d use robot.toml output-dir

rules.message: Created the output dir first: Browser writes playwright-log.txt there and every Browser keyword fails (~16 s each) if it is missing. Relative -d is resolved from the project root, not your cwd.
rules.evidence: B_browser_format.log B01: 3 Browser lines, all FAIL FileNotFoundError, 33 s; S06_relative_d.log: -d rel_out from lab/sub -> ${OUTPUT DIR}=lab/rel_out; smoke run from a subdir resolved to the repo root (~/workspace/rf-mcp-robotcode/out).

rules.fix: quote the delimiter (<<'RF'); only when every `$` in the body is followed by `{` (RF syntax); otherwise deny
rules.message: Quoted the heredoc delimiter (<<'RF'): with an unquoted heredoc the shell expands ${x} to an empty string before Robot sees it.
rules.evidence: S01_unquoted_heredoc.log: `${x}=    Set Variable` -> "No keyword with name '=' found"; `Log To Console    value=${x}` printed `value=` silently.

rules.fix: use single quotes or a quoted heredoc
rules.message: Double quotes let the shell expand ${...} before Robot sees it. Use: robotcode repl --plain -d out <<'RF' ... RF
rules.evidence: S03_echo.log (escaped variant reached RF; unescaped expands to empty like S01).

rules.fix: insert `2>&1` before the first pipe / stdout redirect of the robotcode command
rules.message: Added 2>&1: [ FAIL ] lines go to stderr and were dropped by your pipe/redirect.
rules.evidence: R16_fail_stream: stdout='before\nafter-fail', stderr='[ FAIL ] 1 != 2'; S04_stderr.log: `| tail` without 2>&1 showed nothing. Order is preserved with 2>&1 (combined logs).

rules.message: robotcode repl always exits 0, even after failures; read the [ FAIL ] lines instead. (robot-debug returns the failed-test count.)
rules.evidence: repl_cases.jsonl: rc=0 in all 62 repl cases incl. FAIL; D01 rc=1 (1 failed test), D11 rc=253 (.abort).

rules.message: Positional arguments of `robotcode repl` are FILES, not statements. Feed statements on stdin: robotcode repl --plain -d out <<'RF' ... RF
rules.evidence: S14_misc.log S14c: "Invalid value for '[FILES]...': File 'Log To Console    x' does not exist." rc=2.

rules.fix: move -p/--profile, -c/--config, -r/--root before the subcommand (`robotcode -p dev repl ...`)
rules.message: Moved the profile/config/root option before the subcommand; `robotcode repl -p x` is a usage error.
rules.evidence: S14d: "Error: No such option '-p'."

detect.pattern: robotcode ... repl without heredoc/pipe/< redirect/file argument

rules.message: With no piped input the REPL reads EOF and exits immediately without running anything. Pipe statements via a quoted heredoc.
rules.evidence: S14e: < /dev/null -> exits in 1.2 s, no output.

detect.pattern: repl ... <existing file args>; lint the file with the input rules (I04/I05 especially)

rules.message: A FILE argument is parsed as one block: one syntax error (e.g. unclosed FOR) and NOTHING in the file runs, silently. In files `...` continuation and blank lines are fine. Without -i, stdin is ignored after the files.
rules.evidence: S07_file_args.log: S07b (unclosed FOR) printed nothing, rc 0; S07 continuation folded correctly; S07d stdin ignored; S07c -i reads stdin after the file and keeps its variables.

detect.pattern: body uses page/session keywords (Click, Fill Text, Get Text, Get Element*, Wait For*, GET On Session, ...) but has no Library/New Browser/New Page/Open Browser/Create Session line

rules.message: Each robotcode repl invocation is a new process: browser, sessions and variables from earlier calls are gone. Start the heredoc with Library / New Browser / New Page (and login), or use the persistent session the harness provides.
rules.evidence: process model (one interpreter per invocation); round1 stepwise/findings.md approach C (1.3 s per fresh step, state lost without hacks).

detect.pattern: count of Browser/Selenium locator lines x library timeout > ~0.75 x agent tool timeout (Claude Bash 120 s default)

rules.message: Many locator lines x 10 s timeout can exceed the shell timeout; the REPL then dies with the browser and all output. Keep heredocs short or lower the REPL timeout (see timeout policy).
rules.evidence: B01: 16 s per failing Browser line; a failure never stops later lines (R16).

detect.condition: line has no tab and no run of 2+ spaces, and the longest prefix of words that is a known keyword (libdoc names of imported libs + BuiltIn, case/space-insensitive) is shorter than the whole line

rules.fix: split after the known keyword name with 4 spaces; split remaining tokens on single spaces only when the keyword's arg count matches (else deny)
rules.message: Robot needs 2+ spaces (use 4) between keyword and arguments; with single spaces the whole line is one keyword name.
rules.evidence: R03: "No keyword with name 'Log To Console single-space' found. Did you try using keyword 'BuiltIn.Log' or 'BuiltIn.Log To Console' and forgot to use enough whitespace..."; R06b `${x} = Set Variable 7` -> keyword not found; S14i same at (rdb).

rules.message: A real TAB is a valid separator (R04, S01b printf '\t'); a literal backslash-t from `echo` without -e is not (S03c).
rules.evidence: R04_tab, S03_echo.log

rules.fix: fold each `...` line into the previous statement line (join with 4 spaces); not needed for FILE arguments
rules.message: On stdin each line runs as soon as it parses, so `...` continuation lines run as separate statements. Folded them into one line.
rules.evidence: R07: `${d}  Create Dictionary  a=1` ran alone, then "No keyword with name 'b=2' found"; R08: `Log To Console` failed with 0 args. File args fold correctly (S07).

rules.fix: drop blank lines inside open blocks
rules.message: A blank line inside an open FOR/IF/TRY/WHILE/GROUP submits the half block. Removed blank lines inside blocks.
rules.evidence: R10: "FOR loop cannot be empty. / FOR loop must have closing END." then Variable '${i}' not found + 'END is not allowed in this context'. (A CRLF blank line '\r' does not submit: S14a.)

detect.pattern: FOR/WHILE/IF/TRY/GROUP depth > 0 at end of input (inline IF with a keyword on the same line does not open a block)

rules.message: Block without END: the REPL silently runs nothing for it. Close every FOR/IF/WHILE/TRY/GROUP with END.
rules.evidence: R15c_unclosed_for_eof: empty stdout and stderr, rc 0.

rules.message: Old `:FOR` / `\` loop syntax was removed. Use FOR ... END.
rules.evidence: R39: "Support for the old FOR loop syntax has been removed."

rules.message: Removed markdown fences; they ran as keywords named ```robotframework.
rules.evidence: R23: "No keyword with name '```robotframework' found." (rest still ran).

rules.fix: strip *** Settings ***/*** Test Cases *** headers and unindented test-name lines followed by indented steps; keep `Library/Resource/Variables` lines (aliased); `*** Variables ***` rows -> `VAR` lines; deny for *** Keywords *** (cannot define keywords in the REPL)
rules.message: The REPL is a test body: no sections, test names or keyword definitions. Put user keywords in a .resource file and `Import Resource` it; `Library X` lines are fine.
rules.evidence: R25: '*** Test Cases ***' and 'My Test' -> 2 FAILs, then the step ran; R25c: '*** Keywords ***' + 'My Kw' FAIL and the keyword body ran immediately as steps (no keyword defined); R35b Resource works.

rules.fix: delete the line; for [Setup]/[Teardown] warn that the keyword was NOT run
rules.message: [Tags]/[Documentation]/[Setup]/... are silently ignored in the REPL (a [Setup] keyword does not run).
rules.evidence: R28: no output, no error for [Tags]/[Documentation].

rules.message: A bare ${var} line is an empty keyword call. To show a value use `Log To Console    ${var}` (REPL) or `.pp ${var}` at (rdb).
rules.evidence: R27, D01: "Keyword name cannot be empty."

detect.pattern: a known keyword name appears again as a later cell of the same line

rules.message: Only one statement per line; extra cells become arguments of the first keyword.
rules.evidence: R33 / S14h: "Argument 'stream' got value 'Log To Console'...".

rules.message: (silent)
rules.evidence: R24, S14a, D16: CRLF input worked (values without \r, len('abc')=3).

rules.message: Works in the REPL, but write `IF    cond    Kw    args` (inline IF) so the line can go into a suite unchanged.
rules.evidence: R22: ran, no warning shown; R11b inline IF works.

rules.message: Leading indentation (4/8 spaces) is harmless.

rules.fix: replace with `.exit` (or drop; EOF ends the session the same way)
rules.message: End with .exit (or just end the heredoc). `quit`, `.q`, `:q`, `exit()` run as keywords; `.e` is ambiguous.
rules.evidence: S08_exit_words.log: `exit`/`.quit`/`.exit` end the session; lines after .exit are ignored (R18); EOF ends it equally fast (B02 2.69 s vs B03 2.84 s).

rules.message: Dot-commands take bare names: `.kw Get Text`, `.break Process Item`. Quotes become part of the name and never match.
rules.evidence: R19e: .kw "Log To Console" -> No keywords found; D03: breakpoint at keyword '"Process Item"' never hit. `.kw` exact name is case-insensitive and accepts Lib.Kw (R19b/R19d); a non-exact text is a search grouped by library (R19c/R19f). `.doc` takes an IMPORTED library/resource name, not a keyword (R20, R20b, R20c). Dot-commands work only at a fresh prompt, not inside a block (R21f).

rules.message: Unassigned return values are not printed in the REPL; assign them (`${t}=    Get Title` -> `[ INFO ] ${t} = ...`, cut at ~200 chars). `Log    ${big}` prints the whole value. At (rdb) every keyword prints `=> value`.
rules.evidence: R32 (Get Length -> only library INFO, Set Variable -> nothing); S09 (assignment line 221 chars, `Log` 20,009 chars); B04 Get Page Source assignment truncated with '...'; D10/D14 `=> 'ABC'`.

rules.message: A failing line does not stop later lines; fix the FIRST [ FAIL ], the rest are often follow-ups.
rules.evidence: R16, R10 cascade.

rules.message: Relative Import Resource/Library paths and ${EXECDIR} resolve from the project root; `-s path/to/file.robot` makes ${CURDIR} that file's folder. A missing library prints a ~12-line traceback with PYTHONPATH.
rules.evidence: R34/R35, S12_source_cwd.log, R16d.

rules.message: Get Aria Snapshot logs the whole snapshot at INFO even when assigned (thousands of lines), and `Log ${source}` prints everything. Read the hook's .rf/state/latest/{aria.yaml,source.html,controls.tsv} with Grep instead.
rules.evidence: capture fork: Get Aria Snapshot ~4,200 stdout lines on a 247 KB page, not suppressed by Set Log Level NONE; S09: Log of 20k value printed 20,009 chars; assignment lines alone are cut at ~200 chars (S09/B04).

rules.message: Within one session the FIRST import's arguments win; a later `Library    Browser    timeout=5s` is ignored ('has already imported library ... with different arguments'). Use Set Browser Timeout / Set Selenium Timeout to change timeouts mid-session.
rules.evidence: docs fork failure_rules.json (verbatim REPL message).

rules.message: robot-debug pauses at the first uncaught failure by default (values still in scope). EOF at (rdb) = continue; lines after the run ended are ignored; .abort -> rc 253.
At (rdb) each line is evaluated alone: FOR/WHILE/TRY/multi-line IF fail. Use single keyword lines, inline IF, or Evaluate.
rules.evidence: D09: "FOR loop cannot be empty" / "END is not allowed in this context".

rules.fix: rewrite to Import Library / Import Resource / Import Variables
rules.message: At (rdb) `Library X` is not aliased; use `Import Library    X`.
rules.evidence: D10: "No keyword with name 'Library' found." then Import Library worked.

detect.pattern: `.break <Kw>, <cond>` where <cond> references the keyword's own [Arguments] (resolve via robotcode libdoc / resource parse)

rules.message: Keyword breakpoints stop at the CALL SITE; conditions see the caller's variables. A condition on the keyword's own argument cannot be evaluated and the breakpoint then stops at every call.
rules.evidence: D04 `${i} == 2` stopped once; D05 `${item} == 2` stopped 3x; D07 .s steps into the keyword.

rules.message: Prefer `.pp ${var}` / `.print ${expr}` / `.whatis ${v}` over `.vars` (dumps ~40 lines of all scopes; Local shows '(none)' inside keywords even when args exist). Assignments at (rdb) do not undo the failure you are paused at; `.set` stores strings ('7').
rules.evidence: D07/D12 .vars Local (none) while D13 .pp ${item} -> 1; D14 .set -> '7', run still FAIL; D15 .print/.whatis/${{ }} work.

rules.message: --break-on-failed-test stops after the test ended; keywords there fail with IndexError. Use the default break-on-exception instead.
rules.evidence: S14l: "<class 'IndexError'>: list index out of range".
